experiment: MIC-18 online memory and deferred queries
observation_order: MSB-first binary words; one bit per public phase
update_contract: z[t+1] = F[t](z[t], observation[t]); capacity K at every phase
readout_contract: D(final_state, final_query); final query appears only after all observations
dynamic_memory: At most K codes; ceil(log2(K)) bits suffice to represent each code
static_storage: All transition and decoder tables are counted separately and shared across every word
external_memory: none; no history, current observation bypass, intermediate outputs or retrieval channel
population: Every binary word and every final query in each declared finite task
unit: constructed task family; complete rows within a family are dependent

primary.contrast: unrestricted final-message optimum minus optimum with bounded online updates
primary.physical_dose: same two-code final alphabet; online arm constrains every update
primary.declared_analytical_expectation: A full-history majority encoder may outperform a two-state online controller

constructive_cases: All suffix windows with b=0..J bits; one-code parity constant and two-code XOR parity controller
online_search: Canonical partitions of all prefixes, retaining only partitions reachable by causal updates
independent_search: Enumerate every labeled transition table, then quotient state label permutations
handoff_search: All partitions of complete words into at most K cells; encoder has free full-history access
tie_rule: First lexicographic optimal partition; decoder ties predict zero

resource_guard.on_exceed: abort and retain incomplete status; no optimum claim

preflight.empirical_gate: REDESIGN_OR_PILOT_ONLY; complete finite enumeration supports only its declared domain

scope: Deterministic phase-dependent finite controllers with static tables. Learned recurrent models, generalization, Lean kernel proofs and hardware arithmetic are outside this result.
publication: Draft PRs and a raw evidence archive; no merge
